•Began offering paid rides to customers in Zoox autonomous robotaxis in Las Vegas and started testing in San Diego and Houston. Zoox is now operating in 12 U.S. cities.
•Introduced Built Together, a new $1 billion community investment in U.S. data center communities to provide increased support for priorities communities value most, including free community college and trades training, energy and water efficiency upgrades for schools, community buildings and homes, and flexible annual funding for local priorities like roads, fire equipment, affordable housing, and food security.
•Used its logistics network to donate and deliver 450,000+ emergency supplies to recovery efforts from flash floods in Nepal, wildfires in Washington, and a magnitude 7.4 earthquake in Colombia through its Disaster Relief Program.
•Announced plans to hire more than 300,000 seasonal, part-time, and full-time employees across its U.S. operations this holiday season.
•Announced $1.5 billion+ investment to raise minimum starting pay for U.S. full-time operations employees to $20 an hour, and added a new grocery discount and lifetime banking benefit for its teammates.
Financial Guidance
The following forward-looking statements reflect Amazon.com’s expectations as of October 29, 2026, and are subject to substantial uncertainty. Our results are inherently unpredictable and may be materially affected by many factors, such as fluctuations in foreign exchange rates and energy prices, changes in global economic and geopolitical conditions, tariff and trade policies, resource and supply volatility, including for memory chips, and customer demand and spending (including the impact of recessionary fears), inflation, interest rates, regional labor market constraints, world events, the rate of growth of the internet, online commerce, cloud services, and new and emerging technologies, and the various factors detailed below.
Fourth Quarter 2026 Guidance
•Net sales are expected to be between $240.0 billion and $247.0 billion, or to grow between 12% and 16% compared with fourth quarter 2025. This guidance anticipates an unfavorable impact of approximately 60 basis points from foreign exchange rates. Advertising revenue grew 12% year-over-year excluding changes in foreign exchange rates in the third quarter 2026 impacted by timing anomalies primarily related to Prime Day (and a couple other timing factors). We expect year-over-year advertising revenue to grow in the high teens in fourth quarter 2026.
•Operating income is expected to be between $28.5 billion and $33.5 billion, compared with $25.0 billion in fourth quarter 2025.
•We continue to expect 2026 cash capital expenditures to be approximately $220 billion.
•This guidance assumes, among other things, no impact from energy derivative contract remeasurements, and that no additional business acquisitions, restructurings, or legal settlements are concluded.
Conference Call Information
A conference call will be webcast live today at 2:00 p.m. PT/5:00 p.m. ET, and will be available for at least three months at amazon.com/ir. This call will contain forward-looking statements and other material information regarding the Company’s financial and operating results.

Microsoft’un yerel verideki son iki mali yılı FY2025 (dönem bitişi 2025-06-30) ve FY2026 (dönem bitişi 2026-06-30) olarak karşılaştırılmıştır. FY2025’te yıllık gelir 281724000000 USD, net kâr 101832000000 USD ve net kâr marjı 36.15%; FY2026’da yıllık gelir 331839000000 USD, net kâr 133749000000 USD ve net kâr marjı 40.31% oldu. Marjlar, aynı mali yılın net kârının gelirine oranı olarak hesaplanmıştır. [Source 2] [Source 3] [Source 4]

Gelir, FY2026’da FY2025’e göre yükseldi; son mali yılın yıllık gelir büyüme oranı 17.79% olarak hesaplandı. Şirket, FY2026 gelirindeki artışı Microsoft Cloud’daki büyümeye bağladı; Intelligent Cloud gelirindeki artışta Azure, Productivity and Business Processes artışında ise Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud etkiliydi. More Personal Computing geliri ise Xbox kaynaklı düşüş nedeniyle geriledi; Search advertising büyümesi bunu kısmen dengeledi. [Source 7] [Source 12]

Net kâr marjı FY2026’da önceki mali yıla kıyasla yükseldi. Şirket, satışların maliyetinin Microsoft Cloud büyümesiyle arttığını; brüt marj yüzdesinin ise AI altyapısına devam eden yatırımlar ve artan AI ürünü kullanımı nedeniyle hafifçe düştüğünü, Microsoft Cloud verimlilik kazanımlarının bu baskıyı kısmen dengelediğini belirtti. FY2026 net kârındaki artışın karşılaştırmalı yorumunda OpenAI yatırımlarından kaynaklanan kazanç ve kayıpların etkisi de önemlidir: şirket, cari yıl net kârının bu yatırımlardan gelen net kazançlarla, önceki yıl net kârının ise net kayıplarla olumlu ve olumsuz yönde etkilendiğini bildirdi. Bu veriler kârlı faaliyet gösterildiğini ortaya koysa da nakit, borç ve likiditeyi değerlendirecek bilanço kanıtı mevcut değil; dolayısıyla genel finansal dayanıklılık hakkında kapsamlı bir sonuca varılamıyor. 2026-08-20 tarihli şirket açıklamasında FY2026 için yönetim, Production & Precision Ag net satışlarında yaklaşık 10% düşüş; Small Ag & Turf’ta yaklaşık 15% ve Construction & Forestry’de yaklaşık 20% artış bekliyordu. Bunlar gerçekleşmiş sonuçlar değil, o tarihte açıklanan segment bazlı beklentilerdir; talep veya finansman koşullarının gerçekleşmiş etkisini tek başlarına göstermez. Elde bulunan kanıtlar, 2026-08-20 sonrasındaki daha yeni şirket açıklamasının içeriğini doğrulamaya yetmediğinden bu beklentilerin güncelliği veya son açıklamadaki gelişmeler hakkında kesin bir özet sunulamıyor. [Source 37]

Şirketin belirttiği olası riskler arasında tarım döngüsü ve çiftlik gelirleri, ticaret politikası ve tarifeler, makroekonomik koşullar, faiz oranlarındaki oynaklık ve yüksek faizlerin müşteri güveni, sermayeye erişim ve ürün talebi üzerindeki muhtemel olumsuz etkileri yer alıyor. Bunlar risk ifadeleridir; gerçekleşmiş etkiler olarak sunulmamalıdır. Güncel çeyrek ve son açıklamalara ilişkin tarım ekipmanı talebi ile finansman koşullarının fiilî etkileri ve şirketin nakit-borç-likidite durumu için eldeki kanıt yetersizdir; bu nedenle mevcut bilgilerle bu konularda kesin bir değerlendirme yapılamaz. [Source 37]

The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 – 2 vote:
The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.
Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.
Inflation remains elevated. The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability.
Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

Deeper integration of technology into equipment to enable customers to do more with less remains a persistent market trend. Customers seek to improve profitability, productivity, and sustainability by selecting our equipment and technology solutions. These technologies are incorporated into customer operations across the varied production systems that we serve. While we continue to benefit from the adoption of these technologies, revenue from SaaS products did not represent a significant percentage of our revenues in the periods presented.
Company Outlook for 2026
Large agriculture sales are expected to remain subdued in North America and to soften in South America resulting in decreased sales volume for PPA in 2026 compared to 2025. SAT and CF sales are expected to improve in 2026. Our overall net sales are expected to increase in 2026 compared to 2025, with the anticipated decline in PPA sales more than offset by improvements in CF and SAT.
Agriculture and Turf Industry Outlook for 2026
		●	Demand in the U.S. and Canada for large agriculture equipment is expected to decrease compared to 2025 levels as elevated farm input costs, commodity price volatility, and ongoing market uncertainty continue to pressure demand for equipment.
		●	We expect small agriculture and turf equipment sales to be flat to up slightly in the U.S. and Canada. Solid margins in the dairy and livestock sector and steady demand in residential and commercial mowing continue to support the outlook.
		●	In Europe, the industry is forecasted to be flat. While elevated input costs and challenging weather conditions are pressuring crop farming margins, favorable dairy market margins are expected to continue to provide ongoing support to overall industry demand.

		●	Demand in South America is expected to decrease. Elevated production costs and high interest rates are pressuring farm profitability and impacting equipment demand.
		●	Industry sales in Asia are forecasted to be roughly flat, mainly driven by stable end market demand.
Construction and Forestry Industry Outlook for 2026
		●	Industry sales in the U.S. and Canada for construction and compact construction equipment are projected to be higher compared to 2025. Favorable industry fundamentals are supported by infrastructure, data center, and energy-related projects, as well as continued investment in rental fleets.
